text:
If the value of the integral 

$\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{x^{2}}{(1-x^{2})^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}dx$ 

is $\frac{k}{6}$, then k is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{x^{2}}{(1-x^{2})^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}dx$

Let $x=\sin θ$

$\Rightarrow dx=\cos θdθ$

When x = 0 then sin$θ$ = 0 $\Rightarrow$ $θ$ = 0

When $x=\frac{1}{2}$ then $\sin θ=\frac{1}{2}$ $\Rightarrow$ $θ=\frac{π}{6}$

$\therefore$ $I=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{6}}\frac{\sin ^{2}θ}{(\cos ^{2}θ)^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}\cos θdθ$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{6}}\frac{\sin ^{2}θ}{\cos ^{2}θ}dθ$

$=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{6}}\tan ^{2}dθ=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{6}}(\sec ^{2}θ-1)dθ$

$=[\tan θ-θ]_{0}^{\frac{π}{6}}$

$=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}-\frac{π}{6}$

Given, $\frac{k}{6}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}-\frac{π}{6}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}-π}{6}$

$\Rightarrow k=2\sqrt{3}-π$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
Let a, b, c $\in$ R be such that $a^{2}$
 $+ b^{2}$
 $+ c^{2}$
 = 1. If 
$a\cos θ=b\cos \left (θ+\frac{2π}{3}\right )=c\cos \left (θ+\frac{4π}{3}\right )$,

where
$θ=\frac{π}{9}$, then the angle between the vectors
$a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+c\widehat{k}$ and $b\hat{i}+c\hat{j}+a\widehat{k}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $\vec{a_{1}}=a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+c\widehat{k}$

and $\vec{a_{2}}=b\hat{i}+c\hat{j}+a\widehat{k}$

We know, Angle between two vectors

$\cos α=\frac{\vec{a_{1}}.\vec{a_{2}}}{|\vec{a_{1}}|.|\vec{a_{2}}|}$

$=\frac{ab+bc+ac}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}.\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}}$

$=\frac{ab+bc+ac}{(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2})}$

Given, $a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=1$

$\therefore$ $\cos α=ab+bc+ac$

$=abc\left (\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}\right )$ .....(1)

Given, $a\cos θ=b\cos \left (θ+\frac{2π}{3}\right )=c\cos \left (θ+\frac{4π}{3}\right )=λ$ (Assume)

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{a}=\frac{\cos θ}{λ}$

$\frac{1}{b}=\frac{\cos \left (θ+\frac{2π}{3}\right )}{λ}$

$\frac{1}{c}=\frac{\cos \left (θ+\frac{4π}{3}\right )}{λ}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}=\frac{1}{λ}\left [\cos θ+\cos \left (θ+\frac{2π}{3}\right )+\cos \left (θ+\frac{4π}{3}\right )\right ]$

$=\frac{1}{λ}\left [\cos θ+2\cos \left (\frac{2θ+2π}{2}\right )\cos \left (\frac{\frac{2π}{3}}{2}\right )\right ]$

$=\frac{1}{λ}\left [\cos θ+2\cos (θ+π)\cos \left (\frac{π}{3}\right )\right ]$

$=\frac{1}{λ}\left [\cos θ+2(-\cos θ)\times \frac{1}{2}\right ]$

$=\frac{1}{λ}\times 0$

$=0$

Putting value of $λ$ in equation (1),

cos$α$ = abc(0) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $α=\frac{π}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
Suppose f(x) is a polynomial of degree four,
having critical points at –1, 0, 1. If 

T = {x $\in$ R |
f(x) = f(0)}, then the sum of squares of all the
elements of T is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Critical points = $-$1, 0, 1.

$\therefore$ f'(x) = a(x $-$ 1)(x + 1)x

$\therefore$ f(x) = a$\left (\frac{x^{4}}{4}-\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right )+C$

$\because$ f(x) = f(0)

$-a\left (\frac{x^{4}}{4}-\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right )+C=C$

$a\frac{x^{2}}{4}\left (x^{2}-2\right )=0$

$\therefore$ x = 0, $\sqrt{2}$, $-\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ T = $\left \{0,\sqrt{2},-\sqrt{2}\right \}$

Sum of square of elements of $T=0^{2}+\left (\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}+\left (-\sqrt{2}\right )^{2}=4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
Let $e_{1}$
 and $e_{2}$
 be the eccentricities of the
ellipse, 
$\frac{x^{2}}{25}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$(b < 5) and the hyperbola,

$\frac{x^{2}}{16}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ respectively satisfying $e_{1}e_{2}$
 = 1. If $α$

and $β$ are the distances between the foci of the

ellipse and the foci of the hyperbola

respectively, then the ordered pair ($α$, $β$) is
equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{25}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1(b<5)$

Let $e_{1}$ is eccentricity of ellipse 

$\therefore$ $b^{2} = 25 (1$ $-$ $e_{1}^{2}$) ........(1)

Again for hyperbola

$\frac{x^{2}}{16}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$

Let $e_{2}$ is eccentricity of hyperbola.

$\therefore$ $b^{2}=16(e_{1}^{2}-1)$  ......(2)

by (1) & (2)

$25(1-e_{1}^{2})=16(e_{1}^{2}-1)$

Now $e_{1} . e_{2} = 1 ($given)

$\therefore$ $25(1-e_{1}^{2})=16\left (\frac{1-e_{1}^{2}}{e_{1}^{2}}\right )$

or $e_{1} =$ $\frac{4}{5}$   $\therefore$ $e_{2} =$ $\frac{5}{4}$

Now distance between foci is 2ae

$\therefore$ Distance for ellipse = $2\times 5\times \frac{4}{5}=8=α$

Distance for hyperbola = $2\times 4\times \frac{5}{4}=10=β$

$\therefore$ ($α$, $β$) $\equiv$ (8, 10)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
If the term independent of x in the expansion of

$\left (\frac{3}{2}x^{2}-\frac{1}{3x}\right )^{9}$ is k, then 18 k is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
General term,

$T_{r+1}={}^{9}C_{r}\left [\frac{3}{2}x^{2}\right ]^{9-r}\left (-\frac{1}{3x}\right )^{r}$

$T_{r+1}={}^{9}C_{r}\left [\frac{3}{2}\right ]^{9-r}\left (-\frac{1}{3}\right )^{r}x^{18-3r}$

For independent of x 

18 $-$ 3r = 0 $\Rightarrow$ r = 6

$\therefore$ $T_{7}={}^{9}C_{6}\left (\frac{3}{2}\right )^{3}\left (-\frac{1}{3}\right )^{6}=\frac{21}{54}=k$

$\therefore$ $18k=\frac{21}{54}\times 18=7$

text:
The set of all real values of $λ$ for which the
quadratic equations, 
($λ^{2}$
 $+ 1)x^{2}$
 – 4$λ$x + 2 = 0
always have exactly one root in the interval
(0, 1) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given quadratic equation,

$(λ^{2}+1)x^{2}-4λx+2=0$

Here coefficient of $x^{2}$ is ($λ^{2}$ + 1) which is always positive. So quadratic equation is upward parabola.


[IMG]


So, either f(0)  1

or f(0) > 0 and f(1) < 0

$\therefore$ In both those cases,

f(0) f(1) $\leq$ 0

$\Rightarrow$ 2($λ^{2}$ $-$ 4$λ$ + 3) $\leq$ 0

$\Rightarrow$ $λ\in$ [1, 3]

At $λ$ = 1 :

Quadratic equation becomes

$2x^{2}$ $-$ 4x + 2 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ (x $-$ $1)^{2} = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ x = 1, 1

As both roots can't lie between (0, 1)

So, $λ$ = 1 can't be possible.

At $λ$ = 3 :

$10x^{2}$ $-$ 12x + 2 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $5x^{2}$ $-$ 6x + 1 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ (5x $-$ 1) (x $-$ 1) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ x = 1, $\frac{1}{5}$

In the interval (0, 1) exactly one root $\frac{1}{5}$ present.

$\therefore$ $λ$ $\in$ (1, 3]

text:
If $\int \sin ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{\frac{x}{1+x}}\right )dx$ = A(x)$\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right )$ + B(x) + C,

where C is a constant of integration, then the
ordered pair (A(x), B(x)) can be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, I = $\int \sin ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{\frac{x}{1+x}}\right )dx$

Let $\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{1+x}}\right )$ = $θ$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{1+x}}=\sin θ$

$\Rightarrow$ tan $θ$ = $\frac{\sqrt{x}}{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ$ = $\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right )$

$\therefore$ I = $\int \tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right )dx$

= $\int \tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right ).1dx$

Applying integration by parts,
 

I = $\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right ).x-\int \frac{1}{1+x}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}xdx$

Let $\sqrt{x}$ = t

$\Rightarrow$ $x = t^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ dx = 2tdt

$\therefore$ I = $\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right ).x-\int \frac{t^{2}}{(1+t^{2})(2t)}2tdt$

= $\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right ).x-\int \frac{\left (t^{2}+1\right )-1}{(1+t^{2})}dt$

= $\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right ).x-t+\tan ^{-1}t+c$

= $\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{x}\right ).x-\sqrt{x}+\tan ^{-1}\sqrt{x}+c$

$\therefore$ A(x) = x + 1, B(x) = –$\sqrt{x}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

 (1 $\leq$ i $\leq$ 10) be ten observations of a
random variable X. If 
$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}(x_{i}-p)=3$ and $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}(x_{i}-p)^{2}=9$ 
where 0 $\neq$ p $\in$ R, then the
standard deviation of these observations is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Standard deviation = $\sqrt{Variance}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{\sum x_{1}^{2}}{n}-(x–)^{2}}$

$=⎷\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}(x_{i}-p)^{2}}{10}-⎛⎝⎜\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{10}(x_{i}-p)}{10}⎞⎠⎟^{2}$

[ Standard deviation
is free from shifting
of origin.]

$=\sqrt{\frac{9}{10}-\left (\frac{3}{10}\right )^{2}}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{9}{10}-\frac{9}{100}}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{90-9}{100}}$

$=\sqrt{\frac{81}{100}}$

$=\frac{9}{10}$

text:
If $x^{3}dy + xy dx = x^{2}dy + 2y dx$; y(2) = e and

x > 1, then y(4) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{3}dy+xydx=x^{2}dy+2ydx$

$\Rightarrow dy(x^{3}-x^{2})=dx(2y-xy)$

$\Rightarrow$ $-\int \frac{1}{y}dx$ = $\int \frac{x-2}{x^{2}(x-1)}dx$

$\Rightarrow$ $-\ln y=\int \left (\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x-1)}\right )dx$

Where A = 1, B = +2, C = $-$1

$\Rightarrow -\ln y=\ln x-\frac{2}{x}-\ln (x-1)+λ$

As $y(2)=e$

$\Rightarrow -1=\ln 2-1-0+λ$

$\therefore$ $λ=-\ln 2$

$\Rightarrow \ln y=-\ln x+\frac{2}{x}+\ln (x-1)+\ln 2$

Now put x = 4 in equation

$\Rightarrow \ln y=-\ln 4+\frac{1}{2}+\ln 3+\ln 2$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{lny}=\ln \left (\frac{3}{2}\right )+\frac{1}{2}\ln e$

$\Rightarrow y=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{e}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
The probability that a randomly chosen 5-digit
number is made from exactly two digits is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Sample space = 9 $\times$ $10^{4}$

Case - I

Out of exactly two digits selected one is zero then favourable cases = ${}^{9}C_{1}(2^{4}-1)$

Case - II

Both selected digits are non-zero then favourable cases = ${}^{9}C_{2}(2^{5}-2)$

Probability = $\frac{9(2^{4}-1)+\frac{9.8}{2}(2^{5}-2)}{9\times 10^{4}}$

$=\frac{15+120}{10^{4}}=\frac{135}{10^{4}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
The total number of 3-digit numbers, whose
sum of digits is 10, is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let xyz is 3 digits number.

Given that sum of digits = 10

$\therefore$ x + y + z = 10 ......(1)

Also x can't be 0 as if x = 0 then it will become 2 digits number.

So, x $\geq$ 1, y $\geq$ 0, z $\geq$ 0

As x $\geq$ 1

$\Rightarrow$ x $-$ 1 $\geq$ 0

Let x $-$ 1 = t

$\therefore$ t $\geq$ 0

From equation (1)

(x $-$ 1) + y + z = 9

$\Rightarrow$ t + y + z = 9

Now this problem becomes, distributing 9 things among 3 people t, y, z.

Number of ways we can do that

= ${}^{9+3-1}C_{3-1}={}^{11}C_{2}=55$

Now when 3 digit number is 900 then t = 9, y = 0, z = 0.

And when t = 9, then

x $-$ 1 = 9

$\Rightarrow$ x = 10

But we can't take x = 10 in a 3 digits number. So, we have to remove this case.

$\therefore$ Total number of 3 digit numbers = 55 $-$ 1 = 54.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot

text:
Let S be the set of all integer solutions, (x, y, z),
of the system of equations

x – 2y + 5z = 0

–2x + 4y + z = 0

–7x + 14y + 9z = 0

such that 15 $\leq$ $x^{2}$
 $+ y^{2}$
 $+ z^{2}$ $\leq$ 150. Then, the
number of elements in the set S is equal to
$______$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x-2y+5z=0$ ....(1)

$-2x+4y+z=0$ .....(2)

$-7x+14y+9z=0$ ....(3)

2.(1) + (2) we get z = 0, x = 2y

15 $\leq$ $4y^{2} + y^{2}$ $\leq$ 150

$\Rightarrow$ 3 $\leq$ $y^{2}$ $\leq$ 30

$y\in \left [-\sqrt{30},-\sqrt{3}\right ]\cup \left [\sqrt{3},\sqrt{30}\right ]$

$y=\pm 2,\pm 3,\pm 4,\pm 5$

$\therefore$ no. of integer's in S is 8

text:
If m arithmetic means (A.Ms) and three
geometric means (G.Ms) are inserted between
3 and 243 such that $4^{th} A.M$. is equal to $2^{nd}$
G.M., then m is equal to $_________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given m arithmetic means (A.Ms) present between 3 and 243

$\therefore$ Common difference, $d=\frac{b-a}{m+1}=\frac{240}{m+1}$

$\therefore$ 4th A.M. = a + 4d

= 3 + 4 $\times$ $\frac{240}{m+1}$

Also there are 3 G.M between 3 and 243

$\therefore$ Common ratio (r) = $\left (\frac{b}{a}\right )^{\frac{1}{n+1}}$

where n = number of G.M inserted.

$\therefore$ r = $\left (\frac{243}{3}\right )^{\frac{1}{3+1}}=3$

Given, 

$4^{th} A.M = 2^{nd} G.M$

$\Rightarrow 3+4\times \frac{240}{m+1}=3(3)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{960}{m+1}=24$

$\Rightarrow m=39$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 3rd September Evening Slot
